Base directory for this skill: <PLUGIN>\skills\wiki-setup

# Set up, check and diagnose the wiki

Run the smallest procedure that answers the request. Reports, validation and
diagnosis are read-only: no operation, log, commit, index refresh or repair.
Initialization and recovery require the requested scope; a diagnostic result does
not authorize installing tools, rebuilding indexes, editing content or adding a remote.

## Workflow

1. Resolve the vault and absolute installed helpers from
   [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md), and read vault instructions.
   Confirm the intended target and whether the request is report-only or authorizes
   a particular setup/recovery action. No app is needed for filesystem checks.
2. Select the matching procedure below. Run bounded checks and retain their actual
   exit codes, coverage and output. Distinguish no findings from failed coverage.
3. Explain the diagnosed state and its limits. If repair was not requested, stop
   with the report. Content defects route to
   [wiki-maintainer](../wiki-maintainer/SKILL.md); original documentation to
   [wiki-project](../wiki-project/SKILL.md).
4. Before an authorized mutation, read
   [operation completion](../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md) and
   [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md); inspect existing operation
   state, preserve foreign edits and execute only the requested remedy. Verify
   its result using the relevant check and complete its owned transaction.

## Procedures and examples

- **Initialize:** read [initialization](references/initialization.md).
  Request: “Set up this new vault.” Action: preflight existing files and templates,
  open an operation, run `init.mjs` only when it cannot overwrite customized
  templates, inspect scaffold/health, log and close. Result: usable filesystem
  layout, existing content preserved, app registration and local-only status stated.
- **Validate changed pages:** read [scoped validation](references/validation.md).
  Request: “Validate these authored paths only.” Action:
  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/validate-authored.mjs" --paths-file "<ledger>" --json`.
  Result: checked/skipped counts and exact defects; no repairs or writes.
- **Health and backlog:** read [checks and metrics](references/checks.md#health-and-ingest-backlog).
  Request: “How healthy is the wiki, and how many captures need ingestion?” Action:
  run `health.mjs --json` and `health.mjs --backlog`. Result: open integrity defects,
  coverage and the unsummarized-source count; no ingestion.
- **Freshness or lint:** read [freshness](references/checks.md#freshness-and-drift-coverage)
  or [content lint](references/checks.md#content-lint-report).
  Request: “Report stale pages and unsupported quotations.” Action: run read-only
  stale, drift coverage and scoped lint checks. Result: missing-review/stale pages,
  quote findings and coverage; dates, dispositions and content remain unchanged.
- **Search diagnosis:** read [search diagnostics](references/search-diagnostics.md).
  Request: “Why is search lexical only?” Action: run `search.mjs --health`, inspect
  backend/index state and report the cause. Result: an evidence-based diagnosis;
  displayed remediation commands are not executed without authorization.
- **Capture prerequisites:** read [capture prerequisites](references/capture-prerequisites.md).
  Request: “Check whether this machine can clip a presentation.” Action: inspect
  the PowerPoint converter prerequisites. Result: available/missing tools and
  supported fallback, with no invented capture or automatic installation.
- **App access:** read [app access](references/app-access.md).
  Request: “The native note-open action failed.” Action: inspect the guarded
  adapter's failure and canary result once. Result: the unavailable app action is
  reported honestly; independent filesystem work can continue.
- **Authorized recovery:** read [operation recovery](references/operation-recovery.md).
  Request: “Recover my failed scoped publication.” Action: reconcile the saved
  token, ledger and actual commit, retry only the unfinished step and verify the
  remote. Result: recovered publication or an exact blocker without duplicate edits.

## Best practices

Read-only means no cache-producing embedding evaluation either: use drift
`--coverage` for reports. A healthy graph is not factual verification; index
freshness is not a review date. Preserve failed checks and partial coverage in the
report. Check the current target before retrying an uncertain mutation. Never
remove another writer's token or Git lock to make a command succeed.

## Advanced references

The procedures above are conditional: load only the one the requested check needs.
Bounded embedding evaluation and verification cadence are in
[checks](references/checks.md#bounded-maintenance-evaluation); operation refusals,
Git settings and interrupted purge reconciliation are in
[recovery](references/operation-recovery.md). Follow the original action owner's
authorization boundaries even when setup supplies its diagnostic recipe.

## Done

A report states actual findings, checked scope, skipped/failed coverage and makes
no changes. Authorized setup/recovery verifies the requested effect and accounts
for its transaction/publication state; unresolved work has a precise next action.

19	them out of the way merely to restore them later. Report the exact collisions

21	create only missing folders/files from the bundled templates under the same

26	
27	1. Open an operation **before** scaffolding:
28	   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op relink`.
29	   The fresh-vault exception allows its state directory to exist before the other
30	   folders. Retain the token and owned-path ledger.
31	2. With no differing template collisions, run
32	   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/init.mjs"`. If authorized to complete a
33	   partial scaffold with customized collisions, use the missing-only copy path
34	   described above **instead of running init**, and preserve every existing file.
35	   Record newly written paths, inspect expected `raw/clippings`, wiki content
36	   folders, `moc`, `log`, `_templates`, schema, index and bases. Confirm prior
37	   content bytes are unchanged; distinguish scaffold success from app registration.
38	3. Run the direct [health check](checks.md#health-and-ingest-backlog). Empty content
39	   is expected in a new vault; report scan scope instead of claiming factual health.
40	   Validate any authored pages this task additionally created using
41	   [scoped validation](validation.md).
42	4. Write one relink log, build the exact owned ledger and close through
43	   `op-commit.mjs --op relink --since <token> --paths-file <ledger> --title "Initialize vault"`.
44	   Without Git, report local-only initialization. With an existing configured
45	   upstream and no explicit hold, complete ordinary sync/remote verification.
46	   Do not leave a token open simply because no Git repository exists.
47	5. Relay one-time app setup separately: open the folder as an Obsidian vault,
48	   verify `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" vaults`, and import
49	   `templates/webclipper-template.json` into Web Clipper. Use
50	   [app access](app-access.md) if requested app setup fails. Filesystem health
51	   does not prove the native CLI reaches the app.
52	
53	**Done:** expected files exist, prior content is preserved, the initialization
54	operation is accounted for and publication/local-only state is explicit. If
55	customized template collisions prevent safe progress, report them without mutation.

# Initialize a new vault safely

Read [access](../../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md) and
[operation completion](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md) before
initializing. Resolve the explicit intended root and scoped environment. Never
initialize a guessed directory or create a Git repository/remote just to publish.

## Preflight existing files

Inspect the intended root's existing `AGENTS.md`, schema, index and `_templates/`.
`init.mjs` preserves existing root index/schema/base files, but its recursive
template copy can overwrite same-named files under `_templates/`. Its generic
“existing files are kept” help is not a guarantee for customized templates.

For a new root or one with no template collisions, continue. If templates already
exist, compare them against the installed `templates/_templates/` before running
init. Identical collisions are safe; differing/customized collisions require a
non-overwriting plan. Do not run init over those templates or temporarily move
them out of the way merely to restore them later. Report the exact collisions
and preserve them; if the request authorizes completing the partial scaffold,
create only missing folders/files from the bundled templates under the same
operation, leaving every existing file unchanged. Record those exact new paths.
Do not claim that the helper provided an overwrite-safe mode; it has none.

## Initialize and verify

1. Open an operation **before** scaffolding:
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op relink`.
   The fresh-vault exception allows its state directory to exist before the other
   folders. Retain the token and owned-path ledger.
2. With no differing template collisions, run
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/init.mjs"`. If authorized to complete a
   partial scaffold with customized collisions, use the missing-only copy path
   described above **instead of running init**, and preserve every existing file.
   Record newly written paths, inspect expected `raw/clippings`, wiki content
   folders, `moc`, `log`, `_templates`, schema, index and bases. Confirm prior
   content bytes are unchanged; distinguish scaffold success from app registration.
3. Run the direct [health check](checks.md#health-and-ingest-backlog). Empty content
   is expected in a new vault; report scan scope instead of claiming factual health.
   Validate any authored pages this task additionally created using
   [scoped validation](validation.md).
4. Write one relink log, build the exact owned ledger and close through
   `op-commit.mjs --op relink --since <token> --paths-file <ledger> --title "Initialize vault"`.
   Without Git, report local-only initialization. With an existing configured
   upstream and no explicit hold, complete ordinary sync/remote verification.
   Do not leave a token open simply because no Git repository exists.
5. Relay one-time app setup separately: open the folder as an Obsidian vault,
   verify `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" vaults`, and import
   `templates/webclipper-template.json` into Web Clipper. Use
   [app access](app-access.md) if requested app setup fails. Filesystem health
   does not prove the native CLI reaches the app.

**Done:** expected files exist, prior content is preserved, the initialization
operation is accounted for and publication/local-only state is explicit. If
customized template collisions prevent safe progress, report them without mutation.

1	# Vault access and host commands
2	
3	Resolve the plugin root from the installed `SKILL.md` location, not the current
4	working directory: its containing skill folder's `../../` is the plugin root.
5	From a file in a skill's `references/` folder, use `../../../` instead.
6	Resolve and quote absolute helper paths before running commands. Treat
7	`$ARGUMENTS` as the user's request when the host has not substituted it. A linked
8	skill or reference can be read directly when the host has no skill loader; shared
9	policy does not require loading the maintenance-role entry point.
10	Resolve `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT` (default `~/.wiki-master-vault`; with `WIKI_MASTER_REQUIRE_VAULT=1` set and no vault named, a script stops with exit 2 instead of using the default) and inspect only the expected
11	vault paths needed by the task. Read local `AGENTS.md` and schema before edits. A known root and
12	filesystem access are sufficient for the supported operations below; do not ask
13	the user to restart Obsidian as a prerequisite for all work.
14	
15	## Layout and read scope
16	
17	`raw/clippings/` holds captured evidence; `wiki/{sources,entities,concepts,syntheses,authored}/`
18	holds maintained pages; `moc/` holds navigational maps; `log/` holds one file per
19	operation. Never read, cite or count `.recycle/`; only purge owns it. Reads do not
20	open operations, write logs, commit or refresh indexes. Before any authorized
21	mutation, read [operation completion](operations.md); before quoting or
22	synthesizing, read [evidence](evidence.md).
23	
24	Prefer bounded search and relevant MOCs to the generated catalog. Search
25	diagnostics describe coverage, not relevance: a stale index can omit useful pages.
26	Read current passages and disclose weak or failed channels. Index freshness is
27	distinct from factual review dates.
28	
29	## Choose the supported channel
30	
31	| Operation | Channel and fallback |
32	|---|---|
33	| Read a Markdown page or source | CLI `read path=...`, or read its exact path under the known vault root. |
34	| Search | Prefer `search.mjs` and inspect its diagnostics. If a channel fails, use available results plus bounded filesystem `rg` over `wiki/` and `moc/`; include `raw/clippings/` only for evidence lookup. State missing channels. |
35	| Health, evidence routes, identity, relationships, drift coverage | Bundled filesystem helpers work without Obsidian. Do not gate them on `assertRunning`. Drift embeddings still require their backend. |
36	| Factual freshness report | `stale.mjs` may use CLI discovery or scoped filesystem fallback. Preserve missing-review and coverage diagnostics. |
37	| Ordinary Markdown creation/editing | Use exact-path filesystem edits even when the CLI is healthy, with the same operation, evidence, schema and validation contract. Read current content before editing; preserve unrelated changes. Never pass a whole note body through `content=`. |
38	| Small typed property or app actions | Use the guarded CLI entry point below; filesystem property edits remain available with schema validation. |
39	| Opening a note in the UI, executing an Obsidian/plugin command, app state, live Bases queries | Requires working Obsidian CLI. Report the specific unavailable action; continue independent file work. Do not pretend a filesystem approximation executed an app action. |
40	
41	For CLI calls use `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" <command> ...`
42	or the bundled `scripts/lib/vault.mjs` API. These share an OS-managed lock across
43	agent processes, vaults and plugin copies for the same user. Do not launch native
44	`obsidian` directly or bypass a busy guard; other tools' raw calls are not protected.
45	The guard waits up to 10 seconds for a turn, then fails without sending a request.
46	Command execution has its own 10-second default timeout. Each request is limited
47	to a conservative 2,048-byte UTF-8 JSON envelope and rejects physical CR/LF/NUL.
48	This policy is not Obsidian's documented maximum. If rejected before sending,
49	use filesystem Markdown editing or narrow the read query; do not split a note
50	into many CLI writes or disable the guard. No fallback performs writes implicitly.
51	For unavailable, rejected or uncertain requests, follow the direct
52	[app diagnosis](../../wiki-setup/references/app-access.md#failure-refusal-and-uncertain-mutation).
53	A timed-out mutation has an uncertain outcome: inspect the exact target before
54	retrying or switching channels. Never claim a filesystem fallback executed an
55	app-only action. No fallback implicitly authorizes a write.
56	
57	Validate resolved paths stay under the known root. Restrict searches to explicit
58	content directories; exclude `.recycle/`, dot folders, dependency trees and binary
59	originals. Do not recursively enumerate the entire user profile or scan a recycled
60	topic. Raw bodies remain immutable even during fallback. If target content changed
61	since it was read, reconcile it before writing; do not overwrite concurrent work.
62	
63	## Shell portability
64	
65	Examples elsewhere use `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"` as command
66	notation. Replace the placeholder with the actual installed absolute path before
67	execution, and set the vault for the operation's scope. Do not execute literal
68	angle-bracket placeholders or assume a relative `scripts/` path means the plugin.
69	
70	PowerShell (restore any prior environment value):
71	
72	```powershell
73	$wikiPriorVault = $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT
74	try {
75	  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = 'C:/absolute/path/to/vault'
76	  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/health.mjs'
77	  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Wiki health failed' }
78	} finally {
79	  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = $wikiPriorVault
80	}
81	```
82	
83	POSIX shell (one command's environment only):
84	
85	```sh
86	WIKI_MASTER_VAULT='/absolute/path/to/vault' node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/health.mjs'
87	```
88	
89	For Windows redirector and empty-output diagnosis, read
90	[app access](../../wiki-setup/references/app-access.md#windows-invocation) only
91	when needed. These reporting examples are read-only: no operation or rebuild is
92	needed to answer a question.

# Vault access and host commands

Resolve the plugin root from the installed `SKILL.md` location, not the current
working directory: its containing skill folder's `../../` is the plugin root.
From a file in a skill's `references/` folder, use `../../../` instead.
Resolve and quote absolute helper paths before running commands. Treat
`$ARGUMENTS` as the user's request when the host has not substituted it. A linked
skill or reference can be read directly when the host has no skill loader; shared
policy does not require loading the maintenance-role entry point.
Resolve `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT` (default `~/.wiki-master-vault`; with `WIKI_MASTER_REQUIRE_VAULT=1` set and no vault named, a script stops with exit 2 instead of using the default) and inspect only the expected
vault paths needed by the task. Read local `AGENTS.md` and schema before edits. A known root and
filesystem access are sufficient for the supported operations below; do not ask
the user to restart Obsidian as a prerequisite for all work.

## Layout and read scope

`raw/clippings/` holds captured evidence; `wiki/{sources,entities,concepts,syntheses,authored}/`
holds maintained pages; `moc/` holds navigational maps; `log/` holds one file per
operation. Never read, cite or count `.recycle/`; only purge owns it. Reads do not
open operations, write logs, commit or refresh indexes. Before any authorized
mutation, read [operation completion](operations.md); before quoting or
synthesizing, read [evidence](evidence.md).

Prefer bounded search and relevant MOCs to the generated catalog. Search
diagnostics describe coverage, not relevance: a stale index can omit useful pages.
Read current passages and disclose weak or failed channels. Index freshness is
distinct from factual review dates.

## Choose the supported channel

| Operation | Channel and fallback |
|---|---|
| Read a Markdown page or source | CLI `read path=...`, or read its exact path under the known vault root. |
| Search | Prefer `search.mjs` and inspect its diagnostics. If a channel fails, use available results plus bounded filesystem `rg` over `wiki/` and `moc/`; include `raw/clippings/` only for evidence lookup. State missing channels. |
| Health, evidence routes, identity, relationships, drift coverage | Bundled filesystem helpers work without Obsidian. Do not gate them on `assertRunning`. Drift embeddings still require their backend. |
| Factual freshness report | `stale.mjs` may use CLI discovery or scoped filesystem fallback. Preserve missing-review and coverage diagnostics. |
| Ordinary Markdown creation/editing | Use exact-path filesystem edits even when the CLI is healthy, with the same operation, evidence, schema and validation contract. Read current content before editing; preserve unrelated changes. Never pass a whole note body through `content=`. |
| Small typed property or app actions | Use the guarded CLI entry point below; filesystem property edits remain available with schema validation. |
| Opening a note in the UI, executing an Obsidian/plugin command, app state, live Bases queries | Requires working Obsidian CLI. Report the specific unavailable action; continue independent file work. Do not pretend a filesystem approximation executed an app action. |

For CLI calls use `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" <command> ...`
or the bundled `scripts/lib/vault.mjs` API. These share an OS-managed lock across
agent processes, vaults and plugin copies for the same user. Do not launch native
`obsidian` directly or bypass a busy guard; other tools' raw calls are not protected.
The guard waits up to 10 seconds for a turn, then fails without sending a request.
Command execution has its own 10-second default timeout. Each request is limited
to a conservative 2,048-byte UTF-8 JSON envelope and rejects physical CR/LF/NUL.
This policy is not Obsidian's documented maximum. If rejected before sending,
use filesystem Markdown editing or narrow the read query; do not split a note
into many CLI writes or disable the guard. No fallback performs writes implicitly.
For unavailable, rejected or uncertain requests, follow the direct
[app diagnosis](../../wiki-setup/references/app-access.md#failure-refusal-and-uncertain-mutation).
A timed-out mutation has an uncertain outcome: inspect the exact target before
retrying or switching channels. Never claim a filesystem fallback executed an
app-only action. No fallback implicitly authorizes a write.

Validate resolved paths stay under the known root. Restrict searches to explicit
content directories; exclude `.recycle/`, dot folders, dependency trees and binary
originals. Do not recursively enumerate the entire user profile or scan a recycled
topic. Raw bodies remain immutable even during fallback. If target content changed
since it was read, reconcile it before writing; do not overwrite concurrent work.

## Shell portability

Examples elsewhere use `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"` as command
notation. Replace the placeholder with the actual installed absolute path before
execution, and set the vault for the operation's scope. Do not execute literal
angle-bracket placeholders or assume a relative `scripts/` path means the plugin.

PowerShell (restore any prior environment value):

```powershell
$wikiPriorVault = $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT
try {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = 'C:/absolute/path/to/vault'
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/health.mjs'
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Wiki health failed' }
} finally {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = $wikiPriorVault
}
```

POSIX shell (one command's environment only):

```sh
WIKI_MASTER_VAULT='/absolute/path/to/vault' node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/health.mjs'
```

For Windows redirector and empty-output diagnosis, read
[app access](../../wiki-setup/references/app-access.md#windows-invocation) only
when needed. These reporting examples are read-only: no operation or rebuild is
needed to answer a question.

1	# Completion for vault mutations
2	
3	This is the single shared transaction contract for ordinary authorized vault
4	writes: capture, ingestion, original authoring, content repair, synthesis filing
5	and applied triage dispositions. Read-only search, answers, checks and previews
6	open no operations, logs, commits or refreshes. Purge retains its separate plan
7	and publication approvals and owns its transaction.
8	
9	## Ownership and authorization
10	
11	An authorized wiki edit includes scoped validation, catalog maintenance, log,
12	commit, sync and verified remote publication unless the user explicitly holds it.
13	Finish those steps without another routine permission question. Never create a
14	remote/repository just to satisfy publication. Without an upstream report local-only;
15	a local commit or closed token alone is not publication.
16	
17	Read vault instructions. Preserve foreign edits and immutable raw bodies. A token
18	snapshots existing dirty paths, not later ownership, and does not isolate edits to
19	the same file. Coordinate overlapping targets. On resumption reconcile the saved
20	token, owned paths, log and actual commit before opening another operation; use
21	[operation recovery](../../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md) for details.
22	Never delete a token or Git lock to hide unfinished work.
23	
24	An enclosing operation may own delegated work. Give the worker that token; it
25	records exact paths and validation, never closes or aborts the parent's operation.
26	The named owner remains responsible for scoped publication. Do not close user-held
27	or foreign tokens. If blocked, retain actual state and a durable handoff naming
28	the token, owned files, completed steps, unfinished work and exact next action.
29	
30	## Ordinary lifecycle
31	
32	1. **Open before the first write.** Run
33	   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op <op>` and retain the token.
34	   Create new pages only afterward. Use the existing operation vocabulary:
35	   original project documentation uses `relink`; derived answer filing uses `query`;
36	   discovery, ingestion, lint and relink retain their task operations.
37	2. **Keep an exact ledger.** Pass `--since <token>` to clippers, `log-entry.mjs`,
38	   `index-gen.mjs` and applied `refresh-catalogs.mjs` so they record actual written
39	   paths. Record file-tool edits with
40	   `op-ledger.mjs add --since <token> <vault-relative-path>...`. Use
41	   `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <ledger>` to produce the JSON array for
42	   `--paths-file`, under `.wiki-master/` or outside the vault. Inspect its warnings:
43	   pre-dirty recorded paths, paths no longer dirty and changed but unrecorded paths.
44	   Do not rebuild the ledger from Git's quoted filename display: Unicode paths
45	   can be silently lost. Unclaimed files are not automatically yours.
46	3. **Edit and validate.** Check behavior, schema, canonical placement and exact
47	   citations. Follow direct [scoped validation](../../wiki-setup/references/validation.md)
48	   for changed pages and the relevant [checks](../../wiki-setup/references/checks.md).
49	   Advance `reviewed` only after factual verification; mechanical edits preserve it.
50	   Inspect an uncertain write's actual target before retrying. A failed check
51	   stops completion until its cause is resolved within scope.
52	4. **Refresh affected owned catalogs once.** Generated fences are derived, never
53	   hand-edited. `index-gen.mjs` regenerates the global index while preserving manual
54	   framing. Project documentation uses [project catalogs](../../wiki-project/references/catalogs.md).
55	   A catalog already dirty from another writer remains theirs: use safe project
56	   generators and report deferred global refresh. Record actual changed paths,
57	   rebuild the ledger and rerun validation when the owned set grows.
58	5. **Log once.** Pipe a concise narrative to
59	   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/log-entry.mjs" --op <op> --title "<title>" --since <token>`.
60	   The helper creates one unique `log/YYYY-MM-DD-HHmmss-<op>-<slug>.md` with
61	   date/op/title metadata and records its path. Never append to an aggregate log.
62	6. **Commit and inspect.** Regenerate the ledger and read its warnings, then run
63	   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-commit.mjs" --op <op> --title "<title>" --since <token> --paths-file <ledger>`.
64	   Never stage the whole vault. Verify actual path membership. A failed close
65	   retains the token. An unscoped close is refused whenever another token exists,
66	   of any age; there is no override. Pre-dirty paths require explicit ownership
67	   reconciliation; follow [close refusals](../../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md#close-refusals).
68	   When receipts declare byte/hash integrity, pass their `--evidence-map <file>`;
69	   a mismatch must be resolved before completion, never ignored. The helper tries
70	   semantic index refresh after commit: inspect missing-backend/partial-build
71	   notices using [search diagnostics](../../wiki-setup/references/search-diagnostics.md).
72	   A non-Git vault is local-only, not a successful Git commit.
73	7. **Sync and verify.** `op-commit` never pushes. Run
74	   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs"` after closing, not between
75	   edits. It fetches, rebases, pushes with one rejection retry and verifies against
76	   a fresh fetch. Inspect outgoing commits before publishing; coordinate unrelated
77	   or explicitly held local commits. Verify the operation's commit is included in
78	   upstream; after a rebase locate it through its unique log path and inspect the
79	   resulting path membership. Do not delegate publication to Obsidian Git or the user.
80	   Follow [sync recovery](../../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md#refused-sync)
81	   on failure; never force or guess at conflicts. `--commit-local` is for owned hand
82	   edits outside operations, refuses with any open token, and must not sweep foreign work.

# Completion for vault mutations

This is the single shared transaction contract for ordinary authorized vault
writes: capture, ingestion, original authoring, content repair, synthesis filing
and applied triage dispositions. Read-only search, answers, checks and previews
open no operations, logs, commits or refreshes. Purge retains its separate plan
and publication approvals and owns its transaction.

## Ownership and authorization

An authorized wiki edit includes scoped validation, catalog maintenance, log,
commit, sync and verified remote publication unless the user explicitly holds it.
Finish those steps without another routine permission question. Never create a
remote/repository just to satisfy publication. Without an upstream report local-only;
a local commit or closed token alone is not publication.

Read vault instructions. Preserve foreign edits and immutable raw bodies. A token
snapshots existing dirty paths, not later ownership, and does not isolate edits to
the same file. Coordinate overlapping targets. On resumption reconcile the saved
token, owned paths, log and actual commit before opening another operation; use
[operation recovery](../../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md) for details.
Never delete a token or Git lock to hide unfinished work.

An enclosing operation may own delegated work. Give the worker that token; it
records exact paths and validation, never closes or aborts the parent's operation.
The named owner remains responsible for scoped publication. Do not close user-held
or foreign tokens. If blocked, retain actual state and a durable handoff naming
the token, owned files, completed steps, unfinished work and exact next action.

## Ordinary lifecycle

1. **Open before the first write.** Run
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op <op>` and retain the token.
   Create new pages only afterward. Use the existing operation vocabulary:
   original project documentation uses `relink`; derived answer filing uses `query`;
   discovery, ingestion, lint and relink retain their task operations.
2. **Keep an exact ledger.** Pass `--since <token>` to clippers, `log-entry.mjs`,
   `index-gen.mjs` and applied `refresh-catalogs.mjs` so they record actual written
   paths. Record file-tool edits with
   `op-ledger.mjs add --since <token> <vault-relative-path>...`. Use
   `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <ledger>` to produce the JSON array for
   `--paths-file`, under `.wiki-master/` or outside the vault. Inspect its warnings:
   pre-dirty recorded paths, paths no longer dirty and changed but unrecorded paths.
   Do not rebuild the ledger from Git's quoted filename display: Unicode paths
   can be silently lost. Unclaimed files are not automatically yours.
3. **Edit and validate.** Check behavior, schema, canonical placement and exact
   citations. Follow direct [scoped validation](../../wiki-setup/references/validation.md)
   for changed pages and the relevant [checks](../../wiki-setup/references/checks.md).
   Advance `reviewed` only after factual verification; mechanical edits preserve it.
   Inspect an uncertain write's actual target before retrying. A failed check
   stops completion until its cause is resolved within scope.
4. **Refresh affected owned catalogs once.** Generated fences are derived, never
   hand-edited. `index-gen.mjs` regenerates the global index while preserving manual
   framing. Project documentation uses [project catalogs](../../wiki-project/references/catalogs.md).
   A catalog already dirty from another writer remains theirs: use safe project
   generators and report deferred global refresh. Record actual changed paths,
   rebuild the ledger and rerun validation when the owned set grows.
5. **Log once.** Pipe a concise narrative to
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/log-entry.mjs" --op <op> --title "<title>" --since <token>`.
   The helper creates one unique `log/YYYY-MM-DD-HHmmss-<op>-<slug>.md` with
   date/op/title metadata and records its path. Never append to an aggregate log.
6. **Commit and inspect.** Regenerate the ledger and read its warnings, then run
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-commit.mjs" --op <op> --title "<title>" --since <token> --paths-file <ledger>`.
   Never stage the whole vault. Verify actual path membership. A failed close
   retains the token. An unscoped close is refused whenever another token exists,
   of any age; there is no override. Pre-dirty paths require explicit ownership
   reconciliation; follow [close refusals](../../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md#close-refusals).
   When receipts declare byte/hash integrity, pass their `--evidence-map <file>`;
   a mismatch must be resolved before completion, never ignored. The helper tries
   semantic index refresh after commit: inspect missing-backend/partial-build
   notices using [search diagnostics](../../wiki-setup/references/search-diagnostics.md).
   A non-Git vault is local-only, not a successful Git commit.
7. **Sync and verify.** `op-commit` never pushes. Run
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs"` after closing, not between
   edits. It fetches, rebases, pushes with one rejection retry and verifies against
   a fresh fetch. Inspect outgoing commits before publishing; coordinate unrelated
   or explicitly held local commits. Verify the operation's commit is included in
   upstream; after a rebase locate it through its unique log path and inspect the
   resulting path membership. Do not delegate publication to Obsidian Git or the user.
   Follow [sync recovery](../../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md#refused-sync)
   on failure; never force or guess at conflicts. `--commit-local` is for owned hand
   edits outside operations, refuses with any open token, and must not sweep foreign work.

## Combined close and publication

`wiki-sync.mjs --op <token> --paths-file <ledger> --title "<title>"` performs the
same scoped close, then normal sync and remote verification. It closes only the
given token and cannot combine with `--commit-local`. Without an explicit ledger
it uses recorded paths when available, else the guarded unscoped close; prefer an
explicit ledger, especially for file-tool edits. Success distinguishes the landed
commit and publication. A refused close pushes nothing and retains its token;
`committed, not published:` means the close landed and sync still needs recovery.
Inspect state and retry the unfinished step, not the content or log.

**Done only when** the requested change and owned catalogs are validated, one log
and the scoped operation commit are recorded, and remote publication is verified.
Report holds, local-only results and blockers precisely. Detailed verification,
refusal records, uncertain completion, cleanup and Git settings belong to
[operation recovery](../../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md).

## Exceptions with their own transaction

**Re-clipping:** `apply-reclips.mjs` applies repairs but does not own a commit. Use an enclosing operation with an exact target list and ownership ledger; inspect its returned changed paths. A verified repair, a pending table verification and a quarantine are distinct outcomes. Quarantine may close triage without making evidence citable. See [re-clipping and quarantine](../../../docs/reclipping.md) for selectors, mode overrides and the explicit terminal-failure policy.

- `purge.mjs --apply`, `--restore` and `--reconcile` own their manifests, logs and
  commits. Do not wrap their transaction in a competing commit. Collateral Markdown
  repairs use an ordinary operation after the purge commit. Keep every seed/plan,
  blocking-source and publication safeguard in the purge skill.
- Fresh initialization can open an operation before scaffolding: the helper can create
  its state directory before the other folders exist. Without Git, explicitly report
  local-only initialization; do not manufacture a repository or publish it.
- Starting triage UI only creates machine-local session state; it is not a content
  edit and does not need a commit. Applying dispositions that change tracked vault
  content or pipeline state uses an enclosing or new ordinary operation.

## Executable lifecycle templates

Replace absolute path placeholders, title and narrative with the real task. The
comment marks where the already-authorized edits and checks occur; do not run the
close step after a failed edit/check. These examples assume a configured upstream
and no explicit user hold, so they include the push step. For an explicit local-only
request, omit that step and report the unpushed commit. The close is scoped with
`--paths-file`; to close and publish in one command, replace the `op-commit` and
`wiki-sync` lines with `wiki-sync.mjs --op <token> --title 'Task title'` (add
`--paths-file <ledger>` to scope it explicitly).

```powershell
$wikiPriorVault = $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT
try {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = 'C:/absolute/path/to/vault'
  $wikiOpToken = node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-begin.mjs' --op relink
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not open wiki operation' }
  # Perform authorized edits, validate, and refresh affected catalogs here.
  # Record each page written with your own file tools: op-ledger.mjs add --since $wikiOpToken <path>...
  'Validated task narrative' | node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/log-entry.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since $wikiOpToken
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not log wiki operation' }
  $wikiLedger = Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) "wiki-ledger-$wikiOpToken.json"
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-ledger.mjs' show --since $wikiOpToken --out $wikiLedger
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not build the wiki operation ledger' }
  # Read what show listed as unclaimed before closing. An unscoped close is refused while another operation is open.
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-commit.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since $wikiOpToken --paths-file $wikiLedger
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not commit wiki operation' }
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs'
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Wiki update is committed locally but not verified published' }
} finally {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = $wikiPriorVault
}
```

```sh
(
  export WIKI_MASTER_VAULT='/absolute/path/to/vault'
  wiki_op_token=$(node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-begin.mjs' --op relink) || exit
  # Perform authorized edits, validate, and refresh affected catalogs here.
  # Record each page written with your own file tools: op-ledger.mjs add --since "$wiki_op_token" <path>...
  printf '%s\n' 'Validated task narrative' | node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/log-entry.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since "$wiki_op_token" || exit
  wiki_ledger="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/wiki-ledger-$wiki_op_token.json"
  node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-ledger.mjs' show --since "$wiki_op_token" --out "$wiki_ledger" || exit
  # Read what show listed as unclaimed before closing. An unscoped close is refused while another operation is open.
  node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-commit.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since "$wiki_op_token" --paths-file "$wiki_ledger" || exit
  node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs' || exit
)
```
